Hi Karthik,

Hope you’re well — we’re pulling together the onboarding package for our Q3 SME accelerator (10 startups, 12-week track). We ran Redwood in our pilot cohort and the founders want to try a deeper integration (embeddings + chat flows).

BrightLabs is asking whether Redwood would consider partner-sourced promotional credits (co-funded by BrightLabs + Redwood) to seed 10 trials so the startups can run a meaningful POC before committing. Our ask below:
- Trial length: 90 days per startup
- Per-startup cap: $5,000 equivalent credits (token-based usage)
- Total ask: $50,000 co-funded, BrightLabs covers 50% upfront

I attached the accelerator proposal and the (anonymized) cohort roster. We can provide a short 15-minute joint intro/demo for the founders if that helps adoption.

We’re flexible on routing (marketplace voucher vs partner-managed credits). Can you let us know what information you need for an internal review? We’d like to finalize above-the-line sponsorship by June 8.

Thanks,

Karthik — thanks for the ping and for the clear ask. Quick take: this is the sort of accelerator co-fund we can support, but with a few guardrails.

Eligibility & ops:
- Size & duration are reasonable for a pilot. Recommend starting with 5 startups (50% of total) to validate demand and metric lift.
- Funding model: cofunding via partner-managed vouchers is easiest for BrightLabs (they can distribute codes) but we’ll need a reconciliation file and one activation pass from our side.
- Accounting: finance will require a single PO or a signed partner credit agreement to recognize the cofund. We can do monthly usage reconciliation.

Compliance/legal asks:
- Need confirmation on whether any startups will route PII or regulated data through Redwood. If so, we require the SOC2 attestation and customer-level data retention settings (we can do constrained retention for trials).
- Aditya — can you review the attached proposal and highlight any mandatory redlines? Also flag whether we need a short participant-facing T&C.

Operational timeline:
- If we commit to 5 startups now, ops can create voucher codes and an activation window within 5 business days.
- If approved, propose: Provision 5 vouchers now (worth $5k each), then a conditional top-up for the remaining 5 after usage review (2–3 weeks).

I’ll loop Finance once we have an approval path and the colleague who owns the voucher reconciliation.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Programs Manager

Adding operational details — Vanessa nailed the runbook. A few practicals from the vouchers side: 

- Voucher SKU: we’ll issue 5 x single-use voucher codes (each $5,000 value). Codes expire 90 days from activation. Activation window configurable per cohort.
- Reporting: BrightLabs will get a CSV export of redemptions and per-account spend; we’ll retain detailed logs for finance reconciliation.
- T&Cs: I’ve drafted a short template (one-pager) that covers usage caps, expiration, and data handling for trials. I can share to Maya once legal signs off.

If product ops can spin the codes within 3 business days, we can let BrightLabs start outreach on Monday the 7th — that still meets their June 8 ask for a decision.
